nodes.title: Core practical 8: investigating thermal energy
nodes.description: Core practical 8: investigate thermal energy transfer by conduction, convection and radiation

nodes.title: Lamps & LEDs
nodes.description: know that lamps and LEDs can be used to indicate the presence of a current in a circuit

nodes.title: Calculating work done
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between work done, force and distance moved in the direction of the force: 
work done = force × distance moved W = F × d

nodes.title: Calculating electric charge
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between charge, current and time: charge = current × time 
Q = I × t

nodes.title: Specific heat capacity
nodes.description: know that specific heat capacity is the energy required to change the temperature of an object by one degree Celsius per kilogram of mass (J/kg °C) (physics only)

nodes.title: Scalar & vector quantities
nodes.description: understand how vector quantities differ from scalar quantities

nodes.title: Gravitational potential energy
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between gravitational potential energy, mass, gravitational field strength and height: 
gravitational potential energy = mass × gravitational field strength × height GPE = m × g × h

nodes.title: Production of static
nodes.description: explain how positive and negative electrostatic charges are produced on materials by the loss and gain of electrons (physics only)

nodes.title: Momentum & safety features
nodes.description: use the idea of momentum to explain safety features (physics only)

nodes.title: Kinetic energy
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship: 
kinetic energy = 1/2 × mass × speed2 
KE = 1 / 2 × m× v

nodes.title: Effects of forces
nodes.description: describe the effects of forces between bodies such as changes in speed, shape or direction

nodes.title: Elastic behaviour
nodes.description: describe elastic behaviour as the ability of a material to recover its original shape after the forces causing deformation have been removed

nodes.title: Area under a velocity-time graph
nodes.description: determine the distance travelled from the area between a velocity−time graph and the time axis

nodes.title: Thermistors & LDRs
nodes.description: describe the qualitative variation of resistance of light-dependent resistors (LDRs) with illumination and thermistors with temperature

nodes.title: Core practical 10: investigating changes of state
nodes.description: Core practical 10: obtain a temperature–time graph to show the constant temperature during a change of state (physics only)

nodes.title: Electric forces between charges
nodes.description: know that there are forces of attraction between unlike charges and forces of repulsion between like charges (physics only)

nodes.title: Friction
nodes.description: know that friction is a force that opposes motion

nodes.title: Core practical 11: investigating specific heat capacity
nodes.description: Core practical 11: investigate the specific heat capacity of materials including water and some solids (physics only)

nodes.title: Pressure
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between pressure, force and area: 
pressure = force / area 
p = F /A

nodes.title: Efficiency
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between efficiency, useful energy output and total energy output: 
efficiency = useful energy output / total energy output × 100%

nodes.title: Forces as vectors
nodes.description: understand that force is a vector quantity

nodes.title: Density
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between density, mass and volume: 
density = mass /volume
ρ = m / V

nodes.title: Supporting a beam
nodes.description: understand how the upward forces on a light beam, supported at its ends, vary with the position of a heavy object placed on the beam (physics only)

nodes.title: The principle of moments
nodes.description: use the principle of moments for a simple system of parallel forces acting in one plane (physics only)

nodes.title: Conductors & insulators
nodes.description: identify common materials which are electrical conductors or insulators, including metals and plastics (physics only)

nodes.title: Gradient of a velocity-time graph
nodes.description: determine acceleration from the gradient of a velocity−time graph

nodes.title: Advantages & disadvantages
nodes.description: explain why a series or parallel circuit is more appropriate for particular applications, including domestic lighting

nodes.title: Calculating voltage
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between energy transferred, charge and voltage: energy transferred = charge × voltage 
E = Q × V

nodes.title: Calculating power
nodes.description:
use the relationship between power, work done (energy transferred) and time taken:
power = work done / time taken
P = W / T

nodes.title: Energy resources
nodes.description:
describe the energy transfers involved in generating electricity using: 
• wind
• water
• geothermal resources
• solar heating systems
• solar cells
• fossil fuels
• nuclear power (physics only)

nodes.title: Resistors in series
nodes.description: calculate the currents, voltages and resistances of two resistive components connected in a series circuit

nodes.title: Factors affecting stopping distance
nodes.description: describe the factors affecting vehicle stopping distance, including speed, mass, road condition and reaction time

nodes.title: Solids, liquids & gases
nodes.description: describe the arrangement and motion of particles in solids, liquids and gases (physics only)

nodes.title: Selecting fuses
nodes.description: apply the relationship (power = current × voltage) to the selection of appropriate fuses

nodes.title: Core practical 2: investigating force & extension
nodes.description: Core Practical 2: investigate how extension varies with applied force for helical springs, metal wires and rubber bands

nodes.title: Current
nodes.description: know that current is the rate of flow of charge

nodes.title: Energy stores & transfers
nodes.description:
describe energy transfers involving energy stores: 
• energy stores: chemical, kinetic, gravitational, elastic, thermal, magnetic, electrostatic, nuclear
• energy transfers: mechanically, electrically, by heating, by radiation
(light and sound)

nodes.title: Calculating specific heat capacity
nodes.description:
use the equation: 
change in thermal energy = mass × specific heat capacity × change in temperature 
ΔQ = m × c × ΔT (physics only)

nodes.title: Velocity-time graphs
nodes.description: plot and explain velocity-time graphs

nodes.title: Movement of electrons
nodes.description: explain electrostatic phenomena in terms of the movement of electrons (physics only)

nodes.title: Core practical 9: determining density
nodes.description: Core practical 9: investigate density using direct measurements of mass and volume

nodes.title: Calculating uniform acceleration
nodes.description:
use the relationship between final speed, initial speed, acceleration and distance moved: 
(final speed)2 = (initial speed)2 + (2 × acceleration × distance moved) 
v2 = u2 + (2 × a × s)

nodes.title: Stopping distance
nodes.description: know that the stopping distance of a vehicle is made up of the sum of the thinking distance and the braking distance

nodes.title: Comparing energy resources
nodes.description: describe the advantages and disadvantages of methods of large-scale electricity production from various renewable and non-renewable resources (physics only)

nodes.title: Calculating current, resistance & potential difference
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between voltage, current and resistance: voltage = current × resistance 
V = I × R

nodes.title: Electrical safety
nodes.description: understand how the use of insulation, double insulation, earthing, fuses and circuit breakers protects the device or user in a range of domestic appliances

nodes.title: A.C. & D.C.
nodes.description: know the difference between mains electricity being alternating current (a.c.) and direct current (d.c.) being supplied by a cell or battery

nodes.title: Electrical power
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between power, current and voltage: power = current × voltage
P = I × V

nodes.title: Current in series circuits
nodes.description: understand how the current in a series circuit depends on the applied voltage and the number and nature of other components

nodes.title: Conservation of energy
nodes.description: use the principle of conservation of energy

nodes.title: Centre of gravity
nodes.description: know that the weight of a body acts through its centre of gravity (physics only)

nodes.title: Electricity & heat
nodes.description: understand why a current in a resistor results in the electrical transfer of energy and an increase in temperature, and how this can be used in a variety of domestic contexts

nodes.title: Work, GPE & KE
nodes.description: understand how conservation of energy produces a link between gravitational potential energy, kinetic energy and work

nodes.title: Reducing energy loss
nodes.description: explain ways of reducing unwanted energy transfer, such as insulation

nodes.title: Unbalanced forces
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between unbalanced force, mass and acceleration: force = mass × acceleration 
F = m × a

nodes.title: Work done
nodes.description: know that work done is equal to energy transferred

nodes.title: Distance-time graphs
nodes.description: plot and explain distance−time graphs

nodes.title: Thermal radiation
nodes.description: explain how emission and absorption of radiation are related to surface and temperature

nodes.title: Calculating resultant force
nodes.description: calculate the resultant force of forces that act along a line

nodes.title: Weight
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between weight, mass and gravitational field strength: weight = mass × gravitational field strength 
W = m × g

nodes.title: Pressure in liquids
nodes.description: understand how the pressure at a point in a gas or liquid at rest acts equally in all directions

nodes.title: IV graphs
nodes.description: describe how current varies with voltage in wires, resistors, metal filament lamps and diodes, and how to investigate this experimentally

nodes.title: Uses of static electricity
nodes.description: explain some uses of electrostatic charges, e.g. in photocopiers and inkjet printers (physics only)

nodes.title: Calculating momentum
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between momentum, mass and velocity: 
momentum = mass × velocity p = m × v (physics only)

nodes.title: Charge
nodes.description: know that electric current in solid metallic conductors is a flow of negatively charged electrons

nodes.title: Current in parallel circuits
nodes.description: understand why current is conserved at a junction in a circuit

nodes.title: Dangers of static electricity
nodes.description: explain the potential dangers of electrostatic charges, e.g. when fuelling aircraft and tankers (physics only)

nodes.title: Acceleration
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between acceleration, change in velocity and time taken: 
a = (v − u) / t

nodes.title: Heat & temperature
nodes.description: explain why heating a system will change the energy stored within the system and raise its temperature or produce changes of state (physics only)

nodes.title: Sankey diagrams
nodes.description: describe a variety of everyday and scientific devices and situations, explaining the transfer of the input energy in terms of the above relationship, including their representation by Sankey diagrams

nodes.title: Conduction
nodes.description: describe how thermal energy transfer may take place by conduction, convection and radiation

nodes.title: Voltage
nodes.description:
know that: 
• voltage is the energy transferred per unit charge passed
• the volt is a joule per coulomb.

nodes.title: Hooke's law
nodes.description: know that the initial linear region of a force-extension graph is associated with Hooke’s law

nodes.title: Core practical 3: investigating charging by friction
nodes.description: Core practical 3: investigate how insulating materials can be charged by friction (physics only)

nodes.title: Forces & momentum
nodes.description:
use the relationship between force, change in momentum and time taken: 
force = change in momentum/ time taken
F = (mv − mu) /t (physics only)

nodes.title: Core practical 1: investigating motion
nodes.description: Core practical 1: investigate the motion of everyday objects such as toy cars or tennis balls

nodes.title: Calculating average speed
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between average speed, distance moved and time taken:
average speed = distance moved/time taken

nodes.title: Power
nodes.description: describe power as the rate of transfer of energy or the rate of doing work

nodes.title: The moment of a force
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship between the moment of a force and its perpendicular distance from the pivot: 
moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot (physics only)

nodes.title: Calculating energy transfers
nodes.description:
use the relationship between energy transferred, current, voltage and time: energy transferred = current × voltage × time
E = I × V × t

nodes.title: Convection
nodes.description: explain the role of convection in everyday phenomena

nodes.title: Resistance
nodes.description: describe the qualitative effect of changing resistance on the current in a circuit

nodes.title: Types of forces
nodes.description: identify different types of force such as gravitational or electrostatic

nodes.title: Voltage in series & parallel
nodes.description: know that the voltage across two components connected in parallel is the same

nodes.title: Changes of state
nodes.description: describe the changes that occur when a solid melts to form a liquid, and when a liquid evaporates or boils to form a gas (physics only)

nodes.title: Conservation of momentum
nodes.description: use the conservation of momentum to calculate the mass, velocity or momentum of objects (physics only)

nodes.title: Calculating pressure in a liquid
nodes.description:
know and use the relationship for pressure difference: 
pressure difference = height × density × gravitational field strength p = h × ρ × g

nodes.title: Terminal velocity
nodes.description: describe the forces acting on falling objects (and explain why falling objects reach a terminal velocity)

nodes.title: Newton's third law
nodes.description: demonstrate an understanding of Newton’s third law (physics only)
